messages.content:
A writer revised their English post sentence by sentence. Compare the version before the revision with the final one, as an editor protecting what the writer meant.

Before:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you.” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

Great work! Left kudos~
>>>

Final:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you.” Besides accepting his fate as “captain’s integrity,” as you put it, he also accepts her as his mother and feels grateful for the care she gave him at the end. I’m surprised by that, and I’d love to know how he gets there. Was there even a little regret for what he did to her?

Great work! Left kudos~
>>>

During the revision the writer confirmed what they meant at these places; changes that follow these are intended:
- 「“This is more than I deserve from you.” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?」→ 1. Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
2. 接受命运之外，还有接纳母亲的情感
3. Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
4. 只是惊讶，想探讨他为何接纳

List only real problems in the final version: a point, detail, question or condition from before that is gone (lost); a claim whose meaning changed, e.g. a hedge or a hypothetical that became a flat statement (changed); text that appears twice (duplicated); a sentence that is broken where two pieces were joined (broken). Rewording, reordering and better phrasing are not problems. quote: the exact words from the final version (or, for lost, from before); note: one short Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) sentence to the writer, informal. [] if there is nothing.
Reply with JSON only: {"issues":[{"kind":"lost|changed|duplicated|broken","quote":"","note":""}]}
